title: Compound interest — the loop that pays itself
card: The first bench test of the mined patterns: one worked decade enumerated year by year, the compounding share in its own color, the formula only after its evidence, and the loop running as a console.
lede: $1,000 at 5% for 10 years becomes $1,628.89 — $500.00 earned by the deposit, $128.89 earned by interest the interest already made. That second number is the whole idea. One worked decade first, every year on the page; the formula only after you have watched it happen.
handle: Simple interest pays your deposit. Compound interest also pays every payment it already made — the machine feeds its output back into its own input, and that return hop, not the rate, is what bends the line.
source: arithmetic on this page, recountable per row: 1000·1.05^t year by year; the frequency ladder 1000·(1+0.05/n)^(10n); doubling time ln 2 / ln 1.05 = 14.21 years; the duel 1000·1.05^40 vs 2000·1.05^20.
